You are the test planner in a governed software delivery pipeline. From the approved specification you design the test cases that will prove the service meets its acceptance criteria. You work in parallel with the implementation, so plan against the specification, not against code.

- Cover every functional requirement and every testable non-functional requirement with at least one case; cover failure paths (invalid input, not found, conflicts, expiry, abuse limits) as well as the main path.
- Give each case a stable id of the form `TC-<requirement id>-<nn>`, the requirement it `covers`, its `level` ("unit" for logic in isolation, "integration" for HTTP behaviour through the running Spring context), and a `check` written as a concrete, observable expectation.
- Requirements that cannot be verified by an automated test in this environment (for example a p99 latency target) should still get a case describing the closest meaningful automated check, and a decision explaining the gap.
- `summary`: one line with the number of cases and the coverage.

openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: URL Shortener API
  version: 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT
  description: HTTP API for creating, managing, inspecting, and redirecting short links.
servers:
  - url: /
tags:
  - name: Links
    description: Link creation and management.
  - name: Redirects
    description: Public short-link redirects.
  - name: Operations
    description: Public service health.
paths:
  /api/links:
    post:
      tags: [Links]
      operationId: createLink
      summary: Create a short link
      description: Creates a link and returns its one-time plaintext management token. Creation requests are limited per client peer address. expiresAt is optional; when provided it must be in the future. There is no maximum expiry.
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/CreateLinkRequest'
            example:
              url: https://example.com/article
              alias: article
              expiresAt: '2030-01-01T00:00:00Z'
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Link created.
          headers:
            Location:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/Location'
            X-Content-Type-Options:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/XContentTypeOptions'
            X-Frame-Options:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/XFrameOptions'
            Referrer-Policy:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/ReferrerPolicy'
            Content-Security-Policy:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/ContentSecurityPolicy'
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/CreateLinkResponse'
        '400':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/BadRequest'
        '405':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/MethodNotAllowed'
        '409':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Conflict'
        '413':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/PayloadTooLarge'
        '415':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/UnsupportedMediaType'
        '429':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/RateLimited'
        '500':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/InternalError'
        '503':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/ServiceUnavailable'
  /api/links/{code}:
    parameters:
      - name: code
        in: path
        required: true
        description: Link code or custom alias.
        schema:
          type: string
    get:
      tags: [Links]
      operationId: getLinkMetadata
      summary: Get public link metadata
      description: Returns metadata for a live or expired link. Deleted and unknown links are not exposed.
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Link metadata.
          headers:
            X-Content-Type-Options:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/XContentTypeOptions'
            X-Frame-Options:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/XFrameOptions'
            Referrer-Policy:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/ReferrerPolicy'
            Content-Security-Policy:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/ContentSecurityPolicy'
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/LinkMetadata'
        '404':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound'
        '405':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/MethodNotAllowed'
        '413':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/PayloadTooLarge'
        '500':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/InternalError'
    patch:
      tags: [Links]
      operationId: updateLinkExpiry
      summary: Set or remove a link expiry
      description: |-
        Changes only the expiry of an existing link. Supply expiresAt as an ISO-8601 instant strictly in the future to set it, or explicit null to remove it. The field is required; omission is rejected with 400 and does not change the link. A non-future instant is rejected with 400 and error code invalid_expiry. No update-only maximum expiry is imposed.

        A missing management token returns 401 (missing_token); a wrong token returns 403 (invalid_token), or 429 (rate_limited) when the shared management-token failure limit is exceeded. These failures do not mutate the link. Unknown or deleted links return 404 (not_found). After token authorization, an already expired link returns 410 (expired) and cannot be revived. Successful changes return the updated public metadata. The update takes the existing link-row lock and is committed before the response; subsequent metadata reads and redirect lookups use the persisted expiry.
      security:
        - ManagementToken: []
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/UpdateLinkExpiryRequest'
            examples:
              setExpiry:
                summary: Set a future expiry
                value:
                  expiresAt: '2030-01-01T00:00:00Z'
              removeExpiry:
                summary: Remove the expiry
                value:
                  expiresAt: null
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Expiry updated; the returned metadata contains the new instant or null when expiry was removed.
          headers:
            X-Content-Type-Options:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/XContentTypeOptions'
            X-Frame-Options:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/XFrameOptions'
            Referrer-Policy:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/ReferrerPolicy'
            Content-Security-Policy:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/ContentSecurityPolicy'
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/LinkMetadata'
        '400':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/BadRequest'
        '401':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Unauthorized'
        '403':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Forbidden'
        '404':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound'
        '405':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/MethodNotAllowed'
        '410':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/Expired'
        '413':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/PayloadTooLarge'
        '415':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/UnsupportedMediaType'
        '429':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/RateLimited'
        '500':
          $ref: '#/components/responses/InternalError'
    delete:
      tags: [Links]
      operationId: deleteLink
      summary: Delete a link
      description: Deletes a link into a tombstone. A valid management token is required. Expiry does not prevent deletion.
      parameters:
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/OptionalManagementToken'
      responses:
        '204':
          description: Link deleted; no response body.
          headers:
            X-Content-Type-Options:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/XContentTypeOptions'
            X-Frame-Options:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/XFrameOptions'
            Referrer-Policy:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/ReferrerPolicy'
            Content-Security-Policy:
              $ref: '#/components/headers/ContentSecurityPolicy'
        '401':

<approved_design_notes>
## Components and change

`LinkController` gains `PATCH /api/links/{code}` under the existing `/api/links` base path. It delegates the update to `LinkService`, uses the existing management-token failure throttle, and returns the existing `LinkMetadata` representation. `LinkDtos` gains a request type that preserves the difference between an omitted `expiresAt` and explicit `null`. `Link` gains an expiry mutator; `LinkRepository.lockByCode` is reused for the update. Existing create, metadata, stats, delete, redirect, health, error handling, and filters retain their behavior.

## Data and schema

No schema or migration change is required: `links.expires_at` already stores nullable timestamps at microsecond precision. Expiry updates persist to that column; there is no cache, secondary expiry store, or maximum expiry. The plaintext management token is not returned by the update operation and the stored token hash is unchanged.

## Hot-path flows

**Expiry update:** parse the JSON while preserving field presence; reject omission before calling the service. In a short transaction, lock the link by code, return 404 for unknown or deleted links, authenticate with the existing constant-time token check, reject already expired links with 410 `expired`, and then validate any non-null requested expiry using the creation rule: truncate to microseconds and require it to be strictly after the service clock. Persist the new value (or null), commit, and build the response metadata from the updated link. Wrong-token failures continue through the shared management-token throttle. No mutation occurs for failed validation or authentication.

**Redirect and metadata:** redirect resolution remains the existing database lookup and expiry check, with no new lock or work on the redirect read path. After an update commits, later redirect and metadata lookups read the persisted expiry. Click recording remains best-effort in its own transaction and uses the existing row lock; updates therefore serialize with click recording and deletion. Preserve the redirect controller's behavior of serving the redirect if click recording fails.

## Non-functional requirements and verification

The route is additive and does not change creation limits or existing endpoint contracts. Keep update transactions short to limit lock contention. Cover set, clear, omission, auth failures, expired/deleted links, boundary/far-future validation, redirect behavior, shared throttling, and update races with click recording and deletion. Run existing lifecycle, creation, error/header, click-isolation, persistence, and redirect-latency tests. The API definition belongs at `url-shortener/openapi.yaml`; operator and client documentation at `url-shortener/README.md` and `url-shortener/docs/api.md`; changelog and release-readiness record at the workflow's specified locations.

## Rejected alternatives

- A separate expiry endpoint or a different base path would introduce a competing API convention; PATCH on the existing link resource is additive and matches the approved route.
- Treating omitted `expiresAt` as null would turn an incomplete request into an accidental expiry removal, so omission is rejected explicitly.
- Allowing an expired link to be revived conflicts with redirect expiry behavior; expired links stay expired and updates return 410.
- An update-only maximum, schema migration, cache, or separate persistence path adds inconsistency or complexity without need. Locking redirect resolution would also add avoidable work to the latency-sensitive read path.
</approved_design_notes>

decisions.choice: Use automated file-content and OpenAPI parsing checks for artifact presence and key contract statements, with a human review before shipment.
decisions.rationale: Automated checks can catch missing or structurally incomplete artifacts, but cannot establish that operator/client guidance is sufficiently clear or that a release review was genuinely completed.

decisions.choice: Run the established RedirectLatencyTest as the closest automated regression check.
decisions.rationale: The specification provides no numeric latency target or percentile acceptance threshold for this change; the existing test can detect regressions against the service's current expectation but cannot prove an unspecified target.

decisions.choice: Assert persisted-state and click/tombstone invariants rather than requiring a particular winner in races.
decisions.rationale: The approved design serializes operations on the link row, but does not require which concurrent operation acquires the lock first.

data.summary: 19 cases covering FR1–FR7 and NFR1–NFR3, including endpoint success and failure paths, shared throttling, concurrency, compatibility, and release artifacts.

test_cases.check: PATCH an active link with a valid management token and future expiresAt; assert HTTP 200 and that the response metadata contains the requested expiry.
PATCH an active link with expiresAt explicitly set to null; assert HTTP 200 and response metadata contains expiresAt: null.
PATCH an active link with expiresAt omitted; assert HTTP 400 and verify the persisted expiry is unchanged.
PATCH an active link with malformed JSON or a malformed expiresAt value; assert HTTP 400 and verify the persisted expiry is unchanged.
PATCH an active link without X-Management-Token; assert the established HTTP 401 missing_token response and verify the expiry is unchanged.
PATCH an active link with an incorrect management token; assert the established HTTP 403 invalid_token response and verify the expiry is unchanged.

Send wrong-token PATCH requests until the shared management-token failure limit is exceeded; assert the limit produces HTTP 429 rate_limited and that PATCH failures count toward the same limit as the existing management operations.

Set a future expiry and verify metadata reflects it and a redirect returns HTTP 410 after the controlled clock passes that expiry; then clear a still-active link's expiry and verify a redirect succeeds after the link's former expiry time.

Run expiry update concurrently with click recording through the redirect path; assert the update's expiry is persisted, the redirect remains served, and click recording preserves its expected count and link-state invariants.

Race an expiry update against deletion; assert serialization leaves the link deleted, does not resurrect it, and produces either a completed update followed by deletion or a not-found update after deletion.

For an already expired link, attempt both setting a future expiry and clearing the expiry; assert each request returns HTTP 410 expired, persisted expiry remains unchanged, and redirects remain expired.
On a link that has not expired, submit an expiry equal to the controlled current time and one before it; assert each returns HTTP 400 invalid_expiry and leaves the persisted expiry unchanged.
PATCH a deleted link and an unknown link with a valid token; assert HTTP 404 not_found for each and verify the deleted link remains a tombstone.
Set a valid expiry far beyond commonly expected near-term dates; assert HTTP 200 and that the returned and persisted expiry equal the requested value, with no update-only maximum applied.

Run the existing create, metadata, stats, delete, redirect, health, error-contract, and click-failure-isolation tests; assert their established response contracts, state changes, and redirect behavior remain unchanged.

Run the existing RedirectLatencyTest with the new endpoint tests; assert it continues to meet its established latency expectation and that redirect resolution does not acquire a new lock or perform additional expiry-update work.

Parse url-shortener/openapi.yaml as OpenAPI 3.x and assert it defines PATCH /api/links/{code}, the management-token header, required expiresAt with nullable support, the success metadata response, and the documented relevant error responses.

Check url-shortener/README.md and url-shortener/docs/api.md for the expiry-change operation, authentication, future timestamp and explicit-null request values, omission behavior, and relevant success and error behavior.

Verify url-shortener/CHANGELOG.md contains an entry for this change and url-shortener/docs/releases/1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.md records the release-readiness review as complete, with verification, compatibility, and documentation readiness addressed.
